authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik

standard_prerequisites.name: The theory T_{r,k,mu} and its predicate P, with the relation R on r-tuples of points outside P
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the construction preceding the statement; used inside the counted proof at lines 2354-2355
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the tuple whose existence witnesses the non-forking chain and the relation controlling when a chain has a forking extension.

standard_prerequisites.name: The action of the automorphism group of the model is i-transitive on the complement of P
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 2360-2362
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes each type p_i, for i < r, the unique non-forking extension of p, which is what keeps the first r-1 steps non-forking.

core_obligations: Choose a witnessing tuple: take distinct a_1, ..., a_r realizing p and satisfying the relation R, which is what the definition of non-minimality degree tests (proof lines 2354-2355).

Show the first r-1 steps do not fork: with p_i = tp(a_i / A_{<i}), i-transitivity of the automorphism group on the complement of P makes each p_i the unique non-forking extension of p for i < r (proof lines 2360-2362).

Show the r-th step forks: there are infinitely many choices of a_{r-1}^j producing different lines, and any two of those lines meet only in a_1, ..., a_{r-1} because a further intersection point would make the lines identical, so p_r forks over the empty set (proof lines 2364-2368).
Conclude the degree: a chain of length r with exactly the last step forking exhibits nmdeg(p) = r - 1 (statement and the preceding remarks).
proof_roadmap: Exhibit a chain of realisations of p whose first r-1 extensions are non-forking by i-transitivity (proof lines 2354-2362).
Produce infinitely many incompatible forking extensions at the last step via the lines through a_1, ..., a_{r-1}, and conclude the degree (proof lines 2364-2368).
difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the non-minimality degree of a specific complete type: for the theory T_{r,k,mu} the type p given by the negation of the predicate P has nmdeg(p) = r - 1 (statement lines 2344-2351). The proof exhibits a tuple a_1, ..., a_r witnessing the relation R and analyses the successive types p_i = tp(a_i / A_{<i}): i-transitivity of the automorphism group on the complement of P makes each of the first r-1 a unique non-forking extension of p, while the last step forks because there are infinitely many choices of the final point producing distinct lines that meet the previous ones only in their common points (proof lines 2354-2368). The step that carries the content is the computation of the last step, since it is where the geometry of the lines is used to produce infinitely many forking extensions; the earlier steps are read off from the transitivity assumed in the construction. H2.
